o1.biggest_strength: It aims at the right segment and trigger, opens on the pricing change and the rev rec rebuild, and keeps every step link-free. Each email has a low-friction one-word reply ask, and the 1,900-contact projection is correct (about 130 replies, 65 positive, 55 meetings).
o1.biggest_mistake: It omits the basic compliance pieces (opt-out line, postal address) and does not exclude current customers or open deals.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add an opt-out footer and exclusions for customers and open deals, and move the 9-to-4 proof out of step 1 to keep the opener tighter.

o2.biggest_strength: It is strong operationally: a this-week first move, a clean exclusion table, an opt-out footer, exclusions for customers and open deals, reply handling, and an A/B test plan.
o2.biggest_mistake: Holding step 1 until the 12th to 15th can delay sends by weeks after a pricing flag and weaken the trigger that drove 7.9%. Asking for a 20-minute call from step 1 onward is heavier than a cold finance lead will want.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Send within days of the flag and swap the early 20-minute asks for a one-word reply, keeping the operational extras.

reason: Both found the right segment, trigger and no-link rule. I'd load Output 1 because its emails read more like a peer and ask less of a cold Controller. Output 2's extra ops detail is useful, but its close-window timing risks wasting the pricing trigger.
